metadata.name: Graves' disease (autoimmune hyperthyroidism)
metadata.name_ar: داء غريفز (فرط نشاط الغدة الدرقية المناعي)
metadata.emergency_level: Routine - but thyroid storm is a life-threatening emergency
metadata.severity: Ranges from mild to severe; thyroid storm is critical

overview.short_description: The commonest cause of hyperthyroidism: an autoimmune disorder in which stimulating antibodies drive excess thyroid hormone, causing weight loss, palpitations, heat intolerance, tremor and sometimes eye disease.
overview.detailed_description: Graves' disease is autoimmune hyperthyroidism due to TSH-receptor stimulating antibodies. It presents with a hypermetabolic state, often a diffuse goitre and, distinctively, Graves' orbitopathy (eye disease). Diagnosis is biochemical (suppressed TSH, raised free T4/T3) plus positive TRAb or a diffuse uptake on scanning. Treatment options are antithyroid drugs, radioiodine or surgery, alongside beta-blockade for symptoms.
overview.pathophysiology: TSH-receptor antibodies (TRAb) stimulate the thyroid, causing unregulated hormone production and gland growth. The same/related antibodies affect retro-orbital tissue, causing orbitopathy.
overview.etiology: Autoimmune (TSH-receptor stimulating antibodies); genetic predisposition plus triggers (stress, smoking, postpartum, iodine, some drugs).
overview.natural_history: Fluctuating; may remit with antithyroid drugs in some, but relapse is common; definitive treatment (radioiodine/surgery) often needed. Orbitopathy runs its own course, worsened by smoking.
overview.prognosis: Good with treatment; risk of relapse and of hypothyroidism after definitive therapy; orbitopathy can affect vision if severe.

prevalence.value: The most common cause of hyperthyroidism; affects around 1-2% over a lifetime, much more in women.

incidence.value: Peaks in young to middle-aged adults; strongly female-predominant.

mortality.value: Low with treatment; thyroid storm has high mortality but is rare.

risk_factors.smoking: Increases risk and markedly worsens Graves' orbitopathy.
risk_factors.diabetes: Type 1 diabetes and other autoimmune diseases cluster with Graves'.
risk_factors.hypertension: Not a risk factor (hyperthyroidism can raise BP/HR).
risk_factors.pregnancy: Postpartum onset/relapse; hyperthyroidism in pregnancy needs specialist care.
risk_factors.medications: Iodine/amiodarone can precipitate thyrotoxicosis; recent immunotherapy.

chief_complaints.complaint: Palpitations and weight loss despite good appetite

symptoms.symptom: Eye signs (exophthalmos, lid retraction, diplopia, grittiness)
symptoms.importance: Graves' orbitopathy is specific to Graves' disease

symptoms.symptom: High fever, agitation/confusion, severe tachycardia/arrhythmia (thyroid storm)

negative_findings.why_important: A normal TSH essentially excludes overt hyperthyroidism

negative_findings.finding: No eye signs and a nodular (not diffuse) gland
negative_findings.why_important: Points away from Graves' towards nodular thyrotoxicosis

history_questions.question: Do you have palpitations, weight loss with good appetite, heat intolerance, and tremor?
Any eye symptoms (bulging, grittiness, double vision)?
history_questions.why_ask: Graves' orbitopathy is distinctive to Graves'

history_questions.question: Do you smoke?
history_questions.why_ask: Smoking worsens orbitopathy and affects treatment choice

history_questions.question: Are you pregnant or planning pregnancy?
history_questions.why_ask: Changes drug choice and needs specialist care

history_questions.question: Any severe illness features - fever, agitation, marked palpitations?

physical_examination.examination: Eyes (exophthalmos, lid lag/retraction, movements, visual acuity)

physical_examination.expected_finding: Fine tremor, brisk reflexes, warm moist skin; pretibial myxoedema (rare)

laboratory_tests.test_name: Thyroid function tests (TSH, free T4, free T3)
laboratory_tests.expected_result: Suppressed TSH with raised free T4 and/or free T3

laboratory_tests.test_name: FBC and LFTs (baseline before antithyroid drugs)

imaging.when_needed: When TRAb negative or to distinguish causes of thyrotoxicosis
imaging.expected_findings: Diffuse increased uptake in Graves'; patchy/nodular in other causes

other_diagnostic_tests.biopsy: Fine-needle aspiration only for suspicious nodules

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: Biochemical thyrotoxicosis (suppressed TSH with raised free T4 and/or T3) PLUS evidence of Graves': positive TRAb, diffuse goitre with orbitopathy, or diffuse increased uptake on isotope scan.
diagnostic_criteria.diagnostic_scores: Orbitopathy graded (e.g., clinical activity score) for eye disease.

cutoff_values.value: TSH suppressed below the reference range with raised free T4/T3 defines overt hyperthyroidism; subclinical hyperthyroidism = low TSH with normal free T4/T3.

differential_diagnosis.differences: Older, nodular gland, NO orbitopathy, TRAb negative
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Is the gland nodular and are there no eye signs?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Painful gland (subacute) or postpartum; low uptake; self-limiting
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Any neck pain or recent childbirth?

differential_diagnosis.disease: Anxiety / other causes of palpitations and weight loss

diagnostic_questions.question: Do the thyroid tests show a suppressed TSH with raised T4/T3, and is TRAb positive with eye signs?
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: Suppressed TSH + raised T4/T3 + TRAb/orbitopathy -> Graves'

diagnostic_questions.question: Are there features of thyroid storm (fever, agitation, severe arrhythmia)?

next_best_question.question: What do TFTs and TRAb show, are there eye signs, and are you pregnant or severely unwell?
next_best_question.branching_logic: Confirmed Graves' -> beta-blocker for symptoms + antithyroid drug and specialist referral; storm -> emergency; pregnancy/eye disease -> urgent specialist input

red_flags.immediate_action: Emergency - admit; beta-blockade, antithyroid drugs, iodine, supportive care, treat precipitant

red_flags.finding: Sight-threatening orbitopathy (reduced vision, corneal exposure, optic neuropathy)

red_flags.immediate_action: Manage AF and thromboembolic risk alongside thyrotoxicosis
Urgent specialist care; careful drug choice

referral_criteria.urgent_referral: Thyroid storm (emergency); sight-threatening orbitopathy; hyperthyroidism in pregnancy; severe thyrotoxicosis.
referral_criteria.routine_referral: Confirmed Graves' for specialist management (all patients typically need endocrinology input for definitive treatment planning).
referral_criteria.emergency_referral: Thyroid storm or sight-threatening eye disease.

early: Antithyroid drug side effects (agranulocytosis, hepatotoxicity, rash)

initial_management.supportive_care: Explain the condition and options; smoking cessation (protects the eyes); manage symptoms while arranging specialist care.
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Carbimazole/methimazole-class therapy; Propylthiouracil; Beta-blocker. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_NG145.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Stop smoking (especially with eye disease); eye lubrication/protection if orbitopathy.
initial_management.follow_up: Regular thyroid function monitoring during treatment; watch for relapse and for hypothyroidism after definitive therapy.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: Beta-blocker (e.g., propranolol) for symptom relief. Antithyroid drugs (carbimazole first-line; propylthiouracil in early pregnancy) - WARN patients to seek urgent review and a blood count if they develop sore throat/fever (agranulocytosis). Definitive treatment (radioiodine or surgery) as per specialist. Eye disease managed with the endocrinologist/ophthalmologist.

patient_education.home_advice: Graves' disease is an overactive thyroid caused by the immune system, giving symptoms like a racing heart, weight loss, feeling hot and shaky, and sometimes eye problems. It is very treatable. If you start an antithyroid tablet (like carbimazole) and develop a sore throat, mouth ulcers or fever, stop it and seek an urgent blood test - this can be a rare but serious side effect. If you smoke, stopping protects your eyes.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: داء غريفز فرط نشاط في الغدة الدرقية سببه الجهاز المناعي، ويعطي أعراضاً كتسارع القلب ونقص الوزن والإحساس بالحر والرجفة، وأحياناً مشاكل في العين. وهو قابل للعلاج جداً. إذا بدأت دواءً مضاداً للدرقية (مثل الكاربيمازول) وظهر لديك التهاب حلق أو تقرّحات فم أو حرارة، فأوقفه واطلب فحص دم عاجلاً - فقد يكون أثراً جانبياً نادراً لكنه خطير. وإن كنت مدخّناً، فالإقلاع يحمي عينيك.
patient_education.prevention: No primary prevention; smoking cessation reduces eye-disease risk.
patient_education.warning_signs: Sore throat/fever on antithyroid drugs (urgent blood count), severe palpitations/fever/agitation (storm), or worsening vision/eye pain.

prevention.screening: Test thyroid function in symptomatic patients or with autoimmune/family history.

evidence.evidence_level: High for antithyroid drugs, radioiodine and surgery.
evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by NICE_NG145; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.
evidence.legacy_guideline_strength_pre_v13: Strong - NICE NG145, ATA, ETA (eye disease).
